item.title: Squeak 2.27.4
item.description:
• The chat no longer jumps, flickers or shows a message twice while it updates. Every message has exactly one row from the moment you press Send: a message you send while Claude works is its queued line at once (no card above the composer that later moves into the chat), a steer is a dimmed row at the end of the running turn that turns solid in the same place when the agent reads it, and the reply being written is the running turn's last row, the place the finished reply takes. A randomized test races the host's events, the queue and your presses in 600 orders and fails on any duplicate, reordered, vanished or reappearing row.
  • A queued message is one short line in the chat (its first words, how many pictures, "Queued"). Click it to see the whole message and Steer, Edit or Remove it. Editing changes the words and keeps the pictures.

Also in 2.27.3

  • A message you steer into a working chat shows once: dimmed at the bottom until the agent takes it in, then in its place. It no longer also showed solid at the same time.

Also in 2.27.2

  • Settings › Extensions no longer says "Not in this build" for Claude Code (external), Codex (external) and RasanAI: an add-on is unavailable only when the daemon says so, not when the app has no page for it.
  • "Download automatically" is now off by default: Squeak checks for updates on its own but asks before downloading. Installs that had it switched on by an earlier version are reset once; turn it on again in Settings, About if you want it.
  • A message sent while the agent is working (or a pond member's) now waits in the chat itself, dimmed under its author at the end of the transcript, with Steer, Edit and Remove; when its turn starts, that same row becomes the prompt in place, with no second row and no jump. The stack above the composer no longer repeats it (a small "N queued" note stays when two or more wait).
  • Fixed a message sent while the agent was working showing twice, once solid and once dimmed: the host now keeps the send's id with the queued or steered message, so the dimmed row always becomes the real one.
  • File tabs are remembered: the files you had open in a stream come back after a relaunch, in the order you opened them among the threads, if the file still exists.
  • Switching a Markdown file between Preview and Source keeps your place instead of jumping to the top.
  • You can see what is working at a glance: a folded or open pond shows the working glyph where its count sits when any thread inside is working, the needs-you count (wins over working) or an error mark; the count returns when it is quiet.
  • Streams use a new dot-grid glyph instead of the three waves: still and dim when idle, a soft brightness wave while a thread works, steady amber for needs you and red for an error. It holds one frame under Reduce Motion, and VoiceOver reads "greenroom, 1 working, 1 needs you".
